blocks.text: Rest day — and notice it's God who rested. Rest isn't an interruption of good work; it's the completion of it. 'Finishing' includes stopping. If your weeks have no stopping, you've misread the story: the Creator modeled the cease. Today, actually cease. The work will be there on day one; that's the point of day seven.

blocks.prompt: What would it take for you to truly stop — leave the email closed, the phone down — for one full day? What makes you resist it?
blocks.placeholder: What keeps me from ceasing is...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Teach me the blessing of finished work
Give me a sabbath that completes my hours

verse.text: Your eyes saw my unformed body; all the days ordained for me were written in your book.

blocks.text: The week ends on the long view: some work outlasts your labor. The emails fade, but the colleague you mentored, the quality you stood for, the prayer over the work — those are 'days ordained' work. Keep one eye on the eternal ledger. Your work matters to God not mainly for its output, but for the person it's forming you into.

blocks.prompt: Which part of your workweek will matter in ten years? How does that change how you spend this week?
blocks.placeholder: The work that will outlast me is...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let my work build what outlasts it
Write my days in Your book, One who planned them

intro.text: Money is the most practiced area of the modern life, and the most unexamined in the spiritual one. This week we don't worship money or despise it; we take mastery over it — budget, contentment, and a heart fixed on treasure that doesn't rust.

verse.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

blocks.text: The heart follows the treasure, not the other way around. If you want to know where your heart truly is, don't listen to your words — read your bank statement. This week we let that honest accounting happen, because Scripture uses money as a diagnostic: it shows you, in daylight, what you actually love. Whatever we do this week, it starts with telling the truth about the treasure.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Look at where your last month's money actually went
Ask the honest question: what does that reveal I love?
Bring that answer to God without shame

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Show me where my treasure is — and my heart
Let my money submit to You, not rule me

verse.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, and we can take nothing out of it.

blocks.text: The antidote to the devouring 'more' is godliness with contentment — a rare and, Paul says, great gain. You arrived with nothing and will leave with nothing; that isn't morbid, it's clarifying. Contentment is the ability to enjoy what you have without needing what you don't. It makes freedom possible with any income.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name three things you already have that money can't buy
Enjoy one of them fully today
Let 'enough' be enough — not the enemy's word

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Teach me great gain: godliness with contentment
Quiet the appetite that never has enough

verse.text: The plans of the diligent lead to profit as surely as haste leads to poverty.

blocks.text: Mastery over money is planned, not accidental. The diligent plan; the hasty spend. A budget isn't unspiritual — it's wisdom wearing a spreadsheet. This week, if you don't already, sketch where the money goes: income, giving, saving, living. A plan that makes you steward money instead of being drifted by it is a wall you can eat off.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Write a simple plan for the next month's money
Put a line for generosity in it first
Choose diligence over haste, on purpose

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give me diligence in planning my provision
Make my ledger a place where wisdom lives

verse.text: You cannot serve both God and money.

blocks.text: Jesus draws a hard line: no one serves two masters. You'll love one and hate the other — money and God don't do co-ownership. The surrendered Prime isn't the one who has no money; it's the one for whom money has no master-status. Whatever your balance, the question is posture: is money serving your calling, or are you serving its demands?

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one way money has been bossing you
Put it under God's feet in prayer
Make one financial choice from servanthood, not fear

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: I cannot serve two masters — I serve You
Keep money in its servant role, not the throne

verse.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

blocks.text: Quiz day on money. One diagnostic to remember: treasure reveals heart. Check what you remember about the mastery of money, then keep serving the one Master.

blocks.question: How does Matthew 6:21 connect our treasure and our heart?
options: Treasure is proof we work hard
Where our treasure is, our heart is also
We should hide our treasure
Heart decides to ignore treasure
blocks.explain: 'Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.' Money reveals what we actually love.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let my treasure follow my heart to You
Master my money for Your glory

verse.text: Give me neither poverty nor riches, but give me only my daily bread.

blocks.text: Rest day for the wallet. Agur's prayer is a model of holy moderation: not poverty (tempted to steal), not riches (tempted to deny God), only daily bread. There is a freedom in desiring exactly what God gives, day by day. Sit with that modest prayer today. It's the quiet that breaks the grip of the market's noise.

blocks.prompt: What would 'only daily bread' feel like for you — and what part of your life is trying to be richer than that prayer?
blocks.placeholder: The area wanting more than daily bread...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give me neither riches nor poverty — daily bread
Delight me in simplicity of soul

verse.text: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moths and vermin do not destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.

blocks.text: The week closes my aiming higher: money can be converted into currency that outlives the bank. Generosity, mission, the training of a younger life, the relief of a neighbor — investments in the kingdom are stored where nothing rusts or breaks in. Mastery of money isn't accumulation; it's conversion. Trade the temporal for the eternal, and the flourishing years pay dividends forever.

blocks.prompt: What part of your money could be converted this season into a treasure that thief cannot steal? What's holding it back?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Store my treasure where it cannot rust
Give me the courage of generous conversion

intro.text: The flourishing life is not a solo act. This week we tend the table: friendship, hospitality, and the gift of a home with open doors in a world starving for welcome.

verse.text: One who has unreliable friends soon comes to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

blocks.text: Friendship is a stewardship, not a luxury. Proverbs warns about unreliable friends and celebrates the one who sticks closer than family. As a single adult, intentional friendship can be harder — no school gates, no automatic circles. That's exactly why it must be tended on purpose. Invest in the friends who stick, and be the friend who sticks.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Call, message or visit one friend today
Ask a real question, not a small-talk one
Be the 'sticks closer' friend, not just the respondent

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank You for the friends who stick closer
Make me the kind of friend I need

verse.text: Share with the Lord's people who are in need. Practice hospitality.

blocks.text: Practice hospitality — the verb is 'pursue' in the Greek. Hospitality isn't decorative; it's a discipline. For the single person, the offer of a table is an act of priesthood: your home becomes a sanctuary for the lonely, the young, the single mom, the stranger. You don't need a perfect house or a catering budget. You need a kettle, a chair, and a 'come in.'

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Invite someone over this week — anyone
Open the door to someone society leaves out
Let the table be simple but the welcome be wide

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Make my home a sanctuary of welcome
Let the angels I might host be real, not theoretical

verse.text: As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.

blocks.text: Sharp friends are not the easiest friends. They ask the hard questions, tell you the truth about the relationship situation, call you on the stagnation. Iron sharpens by friction. If all your friendships are comfortable, you're being polished by nobody. This week, lean into one conversation that has some bite — the kind that leaves you sharper, not just smiling.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Ask one friend the question you've been avoiding
Receive the honest answer without defending
Let the friction sharpen you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give me iron friends who sharpen me
Make me a sharpener, not a flatterer

verse.text: Do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have shown hospitality to angels without knowing it.

blocks.text: Abraham's hospitality to three strangers became an encounter with God himself. The Bible treats open doors as a space where heaven shows up. Your home — rented, modest, whatever it is — is an embassy of the kingdom. When it's open, precious things walk in. Don't wait until the house is 'ready' to make it a house of welcome. Ready never arrives.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Open your door to one unexpected guest soon
Watch for the 'stranger' God has put near you
Stop waiting for 'ready' — open the door anyway

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let my home be a place where You visit and I can't tell
Give me the courage of open doors

verse.text: One who has unreliable friends soon comes to ruin, but there is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.

blocks.text: Quiz day on friendship. One proverb, one ordering of your social life: keep the stitchers, be the stitcher. Check what you remember, then go sit with a friend.

blocks.question: What does Proverbs 18:24 say about friends?
options: The more friends, the better
A friend who sticks closer than a brother beats unreliable ones
Friends are a distraction from God
Only family can be trusted
blocks.explain: 'There is a friend who sticks closer than a brother.' Quality and loyalty over volume.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank You for loyal friends in my life
Help me steward them well

verse.text: God sets the lonely in families.

blocks.text: Rest day at the table — and the rest is the reminder that loneliness is not your sentence. God's specialty is placing the lonely in families. Your table is part of that: when you set the lonely in your company, you're co-working with God. If you are the lonely one tonight, the first place to look is the table He's already spread. You are not set outside; you are set in.

blocks.prompt: Who around you is lonely right now — and are you? What would it take to seat either of you at a table this week?
blocks.placeholder: The one God wants at a table is...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Set the lonely in families, starting with mine
Let me both give and receive a seat at a table

verse.text: Now that you have purified yourselves by obeying the truth… love one another deeply, from the heart.

blocks.text: The New Testament's 'one anothers' are a whole architecture of friendship — love, encourage, bear burdens, forgive, honor. The table isn't the main event; the 'one another' that happens across it is. This week's table-setting was practice for a lifetime habit: a flourishing life is a connected life, and connected lives are the visible family of God.

blocks.prompt: Which 'one another' do you most need to practice right now — and with whom?
blocks.placeholder: The one another I'll practice is...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Plant me deep in Your family
Make 'one another' the habit of my table

intro.text: A Prime has something the world is short of: years of hard-won experience. This week is about passing it down — mentoring, legacy, and the quiet discipline of putting your life into someone else's.

verse.text: And the things you have heard me say in the presence of many witnesses entrust to reliable people who will also be qualified to teach others.

blocks.text: Paul's legacy plan is a chain: he gave to Timothy, who entrusts to reliable people, who teach others. Your experience isn't meant to end with you. The mistakes, the lessons, the skills, the gospel — they're meant to be handed to reliable people who will pass them on. Who is your Timothy? If the answer is 'nobody yet,' that's the most strategic gap in your life.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one younger person God has put near you
Offer them something specific (skills, time, a listening ear)
Think in chains: who will they then pass it to?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Show me the Timothy You're handing to me
Make me a reliable link in the chain

verse.text: Silver or gold I do not have, but what I do have I give you.

blocks.text: Peter gave the lame man the one thing he had — and it changed his life. Mentoring doesn't require a title, a course, or a budget. It requires giving what you have: your attention, your story, your presence, your prayers. Some of the most powerful passing-down happens in a car ride, a meal, or a text that says 'I believe in you.' Give what you have.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give one younger person your presence today
Tell them a story of a lesson you paid for
Forget the title; give the attention

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let me give what I have, not what I lack
Multiply what I've received through my giving

verse.text: Above all, love each other deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.

blocks.text: Passing things down means loving people who are still being formed — which means forgiving them when they're immature, inconsistent, or ungrateful. Young adults in the making will drop the ball. 'Love each other deeply, because love covers a multitude of sins' is the instruction manual for mentoring. The days they disappoint you are the days the legacy is actually being built.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Extend grace to the learner who failed today
Remember your own younger mistakes
Let love cover the multitude of mentoring sins

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Give me a deep love that covers much
Use me to form, not just inform

verse.text: But as for you, teach what is appropriate to sound doctrine… teach the older men, the older women… and train the younger men.

blocks.text: Titus gets a whole curriculum of passing down: older men and women teaching the younger how to live. Notice it's not a syllabus of doctrines — it's soberness, love, self-control, kindness, managing a home. You pass down a life more than a lecture. What have your years actually taught you? That is your course material. Teach it by living it where the younger can watch.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Write one 'life lesson' your years have taught you
Live it visibly this week — someone is learning from it
Ask who in your life is watching what you teach

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Make my life a curriculum worth studying
Let the younger learn soundness by watching me

verse.text: Entrust to reliable people who will also be qualified to teach others.

blocks.text: Quiz day on legacy. One chain to remember: hear, entrust, teach. Check what you remember, then go start a link.

blocks.question: In 2 Timothy 2:2, what does Paul tell Timothy to do with what he has heard?
options: Keep it private
Entrust it to reliable people who will teach others
Preach it only on special occasions
Write a book
blocks.explain: The legacy is a chain: entrust to reliable people who will teach others. It must move.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Make my learning move into another life
Keep me faithful in the chain

verse.text: He restores my soul. He guides me along the right paths for his name's sake.

blocks.text: Rest day — because passing things down drains and heals at the same time. Mentoring surfaces your own scars; it exposes the places you still need restoring. The Shepherd 'restores my soul' — restoration is on His schedule, not your performance. Let the act of giving to others open the door for Him to give to you. The teacher is also a sheep.

blocks.prompt: What has the past week's giving exposed in you that still needs restoring? Where do you need the Shepherd to guide you back onto the right path?
blocks.placeholder: The part of me needing restoration...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Restore my soul as I give it away
Guide me back to the right paths

days.title: A race to pass the baton

verse.text: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.

blocks.text: Paul's final summary isn't about trophies; it's about finishing and keeping. The opposite of a missed life is not a famous one — it's a finished one, with the baton handed on. Week by week you're building toward that line: fought, finished, kept. And because you passed it all down, the race continues in hands that aren't yours. That's the Prime vocation — to finish, and to make sure the race finishes with you still in it, cheering.

blocks.prompt: What would 'keeping the faith' look like measured at the end of your life, not the end of this week? What baton is yours to hand?
blocks.placeholder: The baton I must pass is...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let me finish the race and keep the faith
Let my legacy be a race that keeps running

intro.text: Singleness, seen from inside God's kingdom, is not an empty waiting room — it is an undivided devotion. This week we name that gift honestly, and let it turn our aloneness into attentiveness.

verse.text: An unmarried woman or man is concerned about the Lord's affairs, that they may be devoted to him in both body and spirit.

blocks.text: Paul isn't pitying the unmarried; he's describing an advantage. The undivided heart belongs to the Lord's affairs — a devotion 'in both body and spirit' that a divided life can't sustain at the same pitch. This is not a lesser status; it's a specific capacity. The question for a single Prime isn't 'when will I be complete?' but 'what is my undivided heart for right now?'

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one Lord's-affair your undivided heart is for today
Spend one unshared hour on it
Refuse to describe yourself as 'incomplete'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive my undivided heart as a gift, not a gap
Show me what this fullness is for

verse.text: There are those who choose to live like eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. The one who can accept this should accept it.

blocks.text: Jesus names a shocking option: some 'choose' singleness for the sake of the kingdom. The word is 'eunuch' — a person made incapable/choosing not to marry, for a purpose beyond themselves. Jesus dignifies the choice. If singleness is your season (or your calling), reclaim it from the cultural pity: it can be a sanctuary, a staging ground, a sending place — for the kingdom.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: If given, receive your singleness as God's placement
Decide the 'sake of the kingdom' your singleness serves
Talk about your status with dignity, not apology

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank You for the kingdom-purpose of this season
Empty the shame out of my marital status

verse.text: And he said to him, 'You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.'

blocks.text: The whole of you — heart, soul, mind — pointed one direction is an unusual, unmanufactured power. The world fragments the heart into many small loves; the first commandment gathers it back. In a season with fewer demands on your attention, you get to practice whole-heartedness at a level most can't. Don't fritter the gift on distraction.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give God one hour of your whole heart today
Do one thing without checking a screen
Practice loving with all your mind — not just feelings

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Take all my heart, soul and mind
Gather the scattered loves into one direction

verse.text: But I wish that all of you were as I am. But each of you has your own gift from God; one of this kind and another of that.

blocks.text: Paul wishes everyone were 'as I am' — unmarried and free — yet immediately insists it's a gift given to some, not a template for all. That is the grace of it: your singleness is not everyone's answer, but it is your gift to steward. Called gift, it changes from lack to leverage. Treat this season as a package of capacity God chose for you, and open it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name the 'gift' in your exact singleness
Open it — use what it makes possible
Bless, not envy, those with the other gift

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank You for the gift that is mine
Let me steward it, not resent it

verse.text: An unmarried… man is concerned about the Lord's affairs.

blocks.text: Quiz day on the untangled heart. One advantage to remember: the undivided. Check what you remember, then go use the edge.

blocks.question: What does Paul say the unmarried person is concerned about?
options: Their own comfort
The affairs of this world
The Lord's affairs
Their future marriage
blocks.explain: 'The unmarried man is concerned about the Lord's affairs… devoted to him in both body and spirit.'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Consecrate my concern to Your affairs
Use the undivided for Your kingdom

verse.text: Your love is better than life.

blocks.text: Rest day — and honest rest for the single heart includes naming the ache. There are nights your singleness feels like a deficiency and the Enemy whispers 'nobody chose you.' David, in a desert, answered the ache with the most radical line in the psalm: 'Your love is better than life.' Better than the life you thought you needed. Rest in a love that outbids every void.

blocks.prompt: Where does singleness ache in you most? Can you meet that place with 'Your love is better than life' — not as denial, but as the deeper claim?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Say it where it hurts: Your love is better than life
Rest in a love that outbids my voids

verse.text: I have loved you with an everlasting love.

blocks.text: The week ends on the deepest truth: you are not half a person waiting to be completed — you are the object of an everlasting love. 'I have loved you with an everlasting love.' Before any human 'meant to be,' there is the love that meant you from eternity. A heart untangled from the need to be settled is free to be wholly present everywhere God sends it: whole, held, and on assignment.

blocks.prompt: What would change in how you live this season if you truly operated from 'I am loved with an everlasting love' and not from 'I am still waiting'?
blocks.placeholder: If I believed I was held, I would...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let Your everlasting love finish me
Send me out whole, held, and free

intro.text: If and when relationships are pursued in this season, Scripture's word of order is guarding — the heart, the aims, the pace. This week we prepare well-loved boundaries for the pursuit of love, so it builds rather than burns.

verse.text: Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.

blocks.text: The front line of dating is not chemistry; it's gatekeeping. 'Above all else, guard your heart' — because everything flows from it. That means being honest about why you're entering a pursuit: loneliness, conformity, or genuine interest in a person God has placed near you? Guarded hearts pursue from wholeness, not from leakiness.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Audit your motives for what you're currently pursuing
Let sobriety, not speed, drive any next step
Say: 'I guard my heart because everything flows from it'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Set a guard on my heart before I give it
Let my pursuit start from wholeness, not loneliness

verse.text: Finally, brothers and sisters, whatever is true, whatever is noble… think about such things.

blocks.text: Before a relationship exists, your thoughts do. Philippians 4:8 gives the filter for the inner life: true, noble, right, pure, lovely, admirable. The imagination is where relationships are either sanctified or sabotaged. Feed the pursuit with clean, hopeful, realistic thoughts — and starve the fantasy that sets you up for disappointment.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Run today's mental input through the Phil 4:8 filter
Starve one fantasy; feed one true, pure thought
Let your mind be a place a relationship could stand

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Guard my thoughts as I prepare my heart
Fix my mind on what is true and pure

verse.text: But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.

blocks.text: The verse about anxiety is also the verse about singleness: seek first the kingdom, and the 'these things' (including, often, a spouse) are handled by the Father who tends to them. The order matters. A pursuit that displaces the kingdom at the top makes everything wobble. Stay rooted in the Kingdom, and let the relationship be a gift within that seeking, not a rescue from it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Check the top of your priorities — is the kingdom first?
Let one kingdom-task receive your best self today
Trust the Father with 'these things'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Set Your kingdom first in my pursuit
Trust You with the 'everything else'

verse.text: Do not be yoked together with unbelievers. For what do righteousness and wickedness have in common?

blocks.text: If pursuing marriage, the boundary Scripture draws sharply is the yoke: don't be unequally yoked with an unbeliever. The image is two animals pulling one plow — if they don't pull together, the plow goes nowhere. A marriage where the deepest thing isn't shared is the loneliest room in the world. Guarded pursuit asks the faith question early, honestly, and without resentment.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Be honest: is faith the central 'pull' of any pursuit?
Value the yoke over the infatuation
Decide the boundary now, not in the crush

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Keep me honest about the yoke
Let me only move in step with those who love You

verse.text: Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.

blocks.text: Quiz day on the pursuit. One commandment to carry: guard first, pursue second. Check what you remember, then keep the guard on.

blocks.question: According to Proverbs 4:23, why must we guard our heart above all else?
options: Others will break it anyway
Everything we do flows from it
It's the seat of romance only
To look strong
blocks.explain: 'Guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.' The heart is the spring of the whole life.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Keep my guard high as I go
Let my heart be trustworthy to give

verse.text: He leads me beside quiet waters, he refreshes my soul.

blocks.text: Rest day — because pursuit is exhausting and the pause is part of the pattern. The Shepherd not only guides; He pauses beside quiet waters and refreshes. There is such a thing as pursuing too hard, too fast, too loudly; a season of quiet waters is where souls get ready for company. Let this whole day be a pause — no swiping, no planning, just refreshment.

blocks.prompt: What would a deliberate pause from pursuing look like for a week? What is the 'quiet waters' God is leading you beside?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Lead me beside quiet waters
Refresh my soul before it gives itself again

verse.text: Delight yourself in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart.

blocks.text: The week ends with the great surrendering promise: delight yourself in the Lord and the desires of your heart — your actual deep desires — are given to you. It's not a math trick to get a spouse; it's the open hand. When your delight is in God, what you desire begins to align with what He gives. Hold any pursuit with an open palm: if God keeps the desire or provides a person, the delight stays in Him either way.

blocks.prompt: What desire are you holding with a clenched fist? Would you be able to hand it fully to God and still delight in Him?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Delight my heart in You above all
Take my clenched desires and make them open-handed

intro.text: Every flourishing life makes room for honest review. The unexamined life drifts; the examined life stewards. This week we do what Prime is built for — looking back, looking in, and letting God's searchlight show us next.

verse.text: Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts. See if there is any offensive way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.

blocks.text: David doesn't hide from the searchlight; he invites it. 'Search me,' he prays — the heart, the anxious thoughts, the offensive ways. Examining a life isn't self-flagellation; it's self-candor under a loving God. The examined life begins with that invitation, and it ends with being led, not just diagnosed, in the way everlasting.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Pray Psalm 139:23–24 honestly — invite the search
Name one anxious thought and one offensive way
Let the search end in 'lead me,' not just 'show me'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Search me; don't let me hide from Your light
Lead me in the way everlasting after the search

verse.text: Anyone who listens to the word but does not do what it says is like someone who looks at his face in a mirror and… goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.

blocks.text: The mirror test is the heart of the examined life: look, remember, and act. Annual reviews, spiritual retreats, honest friends — they're mirrors. But a mirror that changes nothing is decoration. After this week's looking, the point is one actionable 'do what it says.' Flourishing is a life that acts on what it sees.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Take one honest look in the spiritual mirror
Write down what you see — don't let it fade
Turn one insight into an action this week

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let me not forget what I see in Your word
Turn the mirror into motion

verse.text: Be very careful, then, how you live — not as unwise but as wise, making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil.

blocks.text: The examined life is time-disciplined. 'Making the most of every opportunity' reads as 'redeeming the time' — buying back hours from the drift. You can't redeem time you don't audit. This week, actually look at where the hours went: the scrolling, the obligations, the 'just keeping up.' Wise living cuts what drifts and redeems what remains for what matters.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Audit one full day's hours honestly
Cut one time-waster that steals hours weekly
Redeem those hours for one thing that matters

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Teach me to number my days and redeem them
Make my calendar wiser than my habits

verse.text: Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves.

blocks.text: Paul turns the mirror onto the deepest question: are you in the faith — actually? A Prime examining a life asks not just about habits but about the center. If the center is drifting toward self, success, or safety, the whole person follows. The test isn't anxiety; it's honest course-correction while there's still time to steer.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Ask the real question: is Christ truly my faith's center?
Name where the drift has been mild but real
Steer back today, while there is room

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Examine me for the faith that holds
Bring every drift back to the Center

verse.text: Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves.

blocks.text: Quiz day on the examined life. One discipline to own: look, so you can lead. Check what you remember, then stay in the honest mirror.

blocks.question: How does 2 Corinthians 13:5 tell us to examine ourselves?
options: Through our feelings about Sunday
By whether we are in the faith — test yourselves
By comparing ourselves to others
Only when in crisis
blocks.explain: 'Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith.' Honest, regular self-testing.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Keep me in the honest mirror
Let the examination lead, not condemn

verse.text: Be still, and know that I am God.

blocks.text: Rest day — and there is no examination without stillness. Reflection only works when the water is still enough to see through. 'Be still, and know that I am God' is the posture under all self-review: you are not the one being examined by a disappointed judge, but seen by a God who knows. Stillness lets the anxious noise settle so you can actually hear the answer.

blocks.prompt: What did the week's examination reveal that you'd been too busy or too noisy to see? Sit with it in the stillness.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Still my waters so I can be known
Let the knowing of You steady the knowing of me

verse.text: Because of the Lord's great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail. They are new every morning.

blocks.text: The examined life could crush you if it ended in verdict — so it ends in mercy. Whatever this week's mirror showed you, the deeper truth is: His compassions are new every morning. You are not consumed by your discoveries; you're met by grace. The whole point of looking back is that every morning is a fresh beginning. Flourishing is not perfection; it's repentance that keeps pace with the new morning.

blocks.prompt: What did this week's honesty show you that needs tomorrow's new mercy? Write the one thing you'll hand to God with the new morning.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank You that compassions are new every morning
Let the examined life end in mercy, not verdict

intro.text: Thirteen weeks of tending, and now the flourishing life turns outward. This final week we gather the harvest and point it at the world: fruit that feeds others, and a life arranged to send good further than it goes.

verse.text: This is to my Father's glory, that you bear much fruit, showing yourselves to be my disciples.

blocks.text: The whole season collapses into one glory-line: bear fruit. The vineyard of your life — purpose, boundaries, body, work, money, friends, legacy, undivided heart — was never meant to be beautiful for its own sake. It's meant to bear. Fruit is what others can eat. This week, ask one question over everything: what, this season, has ripened for someone else to taste?

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name the 'fruit' this season has ripened in you
Identify who it is for
Bear it — offer it this week

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let my life bear much fruit to Your glory
Show me the hands my fruit is for

verse.text: If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.

blocks.text: Fruit doesn't happen by striving; it happens by remaining. 'Remain in me' is the secret of every flourishing year: stay connected, let the words stay in you, and the asking, doing, and bearing follow. As the season closes, don't release the branches. Winter will test — the abiding vine has roots deep enough for both.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Renew your 'remaining' in Christ today, consciously
Let one of His words stay in you all day
Keep asking from inside the vine

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Keep me remaining in You past this season
Let Your words stay rooted in me

verse.text: His master replied, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things; I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master's happiness!'

blocks.text: The aspiration of the flourishing life, finally, is a Master's 'well done.' Not applause — the approval of the One who gave you the talents. He started you with 'a few things' and watches how you steward them. Faithful with the few — that's the entire exam. The Prime years are time to be faithful with the few so the 'many things' are safe in your hands.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Take stock of your 'few things' with fresh gratitude
Steward them today with the Master in view
Let 'well done' be the audience you work for

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Make me faithful in the few things You gave
Let me meet You at 'well done'

verse.text: Therefore, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.

blocks.text: Flourishing has an endurance clause: stand firm, let nothing move you. The Enemy's favorite tactic in the flourishing years is a slow drift disguised as a short-cut. Steadiness is spiritual stamina. And the verse's engine is the last clause — your labor in the Lord is not in vain. Nothing you've built this season in Him is wasted, even what looks small.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Stand firm on one point the season taught you
Let 'not in vain' fuel today's work
Refuse the shortcut that would move you

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Hold me steady at the season's close
Confirm: my labor in You is not in vain

verse.text: This is to my Father's glory, that you bear much fruit.

blocks.text: Quiz day on the harvest. One line to end on: the fruit is for His glory. Check what you remember of this season's truths, then take the harvest onward.

blocks.question: According to John 15:8, what brings glory to the Father?
options: Being busy for God
Bearing much fruit as disciples
Being approved by people
Avoiding mistakes
blocks.explain: 'This is to my Father's glory, that you bear much fruit, showing yourselves to be my disciples.'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Gather every fruit this season for Your glory
Send me onward with fruit in hand

verse.text: Surely your goodness and love will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the Lord forever.

blocks.text: Rest day at the end of the season — and the shepherd psalm closes with the whole flourishing life in one verse: goodness and love following all your days, a house in the Lord forever. Everything you've tended this spring has been inside that promise. So rest well. The season ends the way it began — with a Shepherd, a table, and the certainty that the goodness follows.

blocks.prompt: Which week of this study most changed how you'll live? What is the one 'flourish' you're carrying out of spring?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank You for the goodness that follows me
Let me dwell in Your house, house of the season and forever

verse.text: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, 'Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?' And I said, 'Here am I. Send me!'

blocks.text: The flourishing years were never the destination; they were the staging ground. The season's last word is a sending: 'Whom shall I send?' The cultivated life, the trained body, the steward's soul, the open table, the passed-down legacy — all of it answers, 'Here am I. Send me.' Go out of this season as you came in — present, and offering: here am I, send me.

blocks.prompt: Where is this season sending you? Say your 'here am I' out loud — to your work, your family, your city, your God.
blocks.placeholder: Here am I; send me to...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Here am I; send me
Let the flourishing years end in a sending, not an ending

title: Pulse — Spring 2026
coverLines: The Jesus Way, one pulse at a time
Thirteen weeks with the same footsteps
March steady, live loud
summary: Spring 2026 study guide for Pulse: thirteen weeks of walking the Jesus way — the same footsteps as Surge, one verse and one daily read for every day of the season.

blocks.text: How to use this study guide

This is a study guide for Pulse. This season Pulse walks the same Jesus Way as Surge — the way, the truth and the life, one step a day — because the beat of a young-adult life is only as steady as the rhythm it keeps. Each week has a theme and a verse for every day. Day 5 is a short quiz; days 6 and 7 are rest and reflection days. Read the verse, chew the lines, do the step, say the prayer. By winter you'll feel the difference in your pace.
Same steps, your cadence

Discipleship is the same road for every generation: deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow (Matthew 16:24). Pulse walks it with the urgency of the young — feet wanting to run. This season is the walkway: thirteen weeks that trade the sprint of passion for the sureness of footsteps that last. Keep the cadence.

intro.text: Every road begins with a call. Before the Jesus way is a set of teachings, it is a person saying 'come and see'. This week we start where the disciples started — at the invitation, not the syllabus.

verse.text: Come, and you will see.

blocks.text: Jesus' first recorded invitation is not a doctrine test but an open door: come and see. Andrew and the other disciple go, they stay, and their whole lives reroute. Following Jesus begins the same way for everyone — not with having it all figured out, but with showing up to look.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Act on 'come and see': actually show up to look at Jesus today
Spend ten minutes in one gospel, not as study — as seeing
Ask one honest question you've been afraid to bring to him

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Answer the call: Lord, I'm coming to see
Ask him to show you what you're walking toward

verse.text: "Come, follow me," Jesus said, "and I will send you out to fish for people."

blocks.text: Jesus calls fishermen into a new trade: fishing for people. The striking thing is that he calls them forward into a mission they don't understand yet — and they leave the nets on the shore. The call promises direction more than detail.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one net on your shore — something safe you're holding back from
Ask: what is Jesus actually inviting me into right now?
Take one step of yes today, even without the full map

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Say yes to his direction before you see his detail
Ask for the same courage the fishermen had

verse.text: So they left everything and followed him.

blocks.text: Luke adds the fuller cost: they left everything. Not a little. Everything. The call of Jesus is not to upgrade your life but to re-own it — from a thing you manage to a thing he sends. Leaving everything usually looks less dramatic and is no less real.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Make a short list of what 'everything' looks like for you this season
Choose one thing to place in his hands that you've been gripping
Don't romanticise it — just do the actual handover

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Hand Jesus the thing you've been managing
Thank him that what you leave is never loss

verse.text: Jesus looked at him and loved him.

blocks.text: Before the rich man gets the hardest invitation in the gospels — go, sell, give, come — he is looked at and loved. The call of Jesus is never a rejection notice. It can be costly; it is never cold.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Receive that look today: Jesus looks at you and loves you
Separate the cost of the call from the love behind it
Let his love give you the courage to hear the costly part honestly

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let Jesus look at you and love you first
Ask for courage to hear the full invitation

verse.text: You still lack one thing.

blocks.text: The rich young man has kept the rules, and Jesus names the gap: one thing — his money owns him, and he walks away sad. Today's quiz tests what we're really attached to when the call gets specific.

blocks.question: Why did Jesus tell the rich young man to sell what he had?
options: Because money is bad and must be destroyed
Because that one possession stood between him and following
blocks.explain: Right — the command was precision medicine. The 'one thing' was the one thing in the way.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to name your 'one thing' honestly
Pray for the courage to loosen your hold on it

verse.text: If you hold to my teaching, you are really my disciples.

blocks.text: The road is not walked in a day; it is walked by holding to his teaching — a verb that means staying, remaining, abiding. On a rest day, let the pace slow. The call was never 'arrive'; it was 'abide'.

blocks.prompt: What has the week's call surfaced that you need to sit with — not solve yet? Write it in one honest paragraph.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to abide in his teaching today
Thank him that discipleship is a staying, not a sprinting

days.title: Written in the book of life

verse.text: Instead, rejoice that your names are written in heaven.

blocks.text: The seventy return from mission amazed at their power, and Jesus redirects their joy: the real wonder is not what you can do but whose you are — your name written in heaven. On Monday, set your anchor on identity before activity.

blocks.prompt: Before the week's doing starts: what does it mean to you that your name is written in heaven? Write it down.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rejoice that your name is written in heaven
Ask him to order your doing after your belonging

intro.text: The Beatitudes are the blueprint of the Jesus way — blessings, not conditions. This week we lay the foundations that the rest of the road is built on.

verse.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

blocks.text: The beatitudes begin at the bottom, not the top: blessed are the poor in spirit — those who admit they don't have enough strength, wisdom or holiness to save themselves. It's the opposite of spiritual hustling. The kingdom is for the people who know they need it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Admit one small poverty out loud: somewhere you simply don't have it
Stop performing spiritual competence with God today
Notice the relief in being poor in spirit before him

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Come to God in your poverty, not your impressive
Thank him that the kingdom goes to the empty-handed

verse.text: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

blocks.text: Jesus blesses mourners at the front of his manifesto — a culture-changing act. Grief over what's broken, what's lost, what's wrong in the world is not a failure of faith; it is the precondition for comfort. You can't be comforted for something you refuse to feel.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let yourself actually grieve one thing — there are no points for stoic
Refuse the cynicism that turns grief into jokes
Ours is the God who promises comfort, not just lectures

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Bring your mourning to the God who comforts
Ask for comfort — real comfort — not just distraction

verse.text: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

blocks.text: Meekness has been misread as weakness, but it is strength under control — a stallion when it could be a bulldozer. The meek inherit the earth because they don't have to conquer it; they know the earth already belongs to God and are content to receive it.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Hold your strength in check in one situation where you could crush
Give up being the smartest person in the room
Be content to inherit rather than to conquer

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the meekness of strength under control
Thank God that the earth is his to give

verse.text: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.

blocks.text: Righteousness is not a distant cool concept here — it is the one thing you want as badly as food and water. Jesus blesses raw appetite. A craving for what's right — in you, in your city, in your workplace — is the sign of a healthy soul, and Jesus promises it gets satisfied.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let yourself actually want what is right — don't apologise for the appetite
Do one righteous (not just legal) thing today
Ask for more hunger, not less

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Bring your hunger for rightness to Jesus
Trust his promise: you will be filled

verse.text: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.

blocks.text: The beatitudes keep going lower: mercy. The merciful are those who have been hurt and choose not to scoreboard it. Today's quiz checks which road actually leads to the heart of the beatitudes.

blocks.question: Why does the 'way of Jesus' start with blessings on the meek and poor in spirit?
options: Because the way is built on receiving, not achieving
Because God admires self-made strength
blocks.explain: Right — the whole way of Jesus is grounded in grace: blessed are the people who come empty, not the ones who compete their way up.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to grow mercy in you the way it grew in him
Thank him that mercy is received before it is given

verse.text: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.

blocks.text: Purity of heart is not perfection of record; it is singleness of intention — one thing you want above the clutter. On a rest day, let the filters settle. What is the one thing you actually want? The pure in heart are on the way to seeing God.

blocks.prompt: Confession moment: what is competing with God for your heart's singularity? Write it down and give it a name.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for a clean, single-hearted desire
Anticipate the blessing: you will see God

verse.text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

blocks.text: The foundation week closes with the family resemblance: peacemakers are called children of God because they act like their Father, who makes peace. On Monday, go make peace in one place — not by winning, by building.

blocks.prompt: Where is there a broken peace you can begin building today — an apology, a bridge, an honest conversation? Write your next step.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to bear your Father's family likeness today
Thank him that peacemakers are his own

intro.text: The world climbs; the Jesus way descends. This week we walk the radical centre of Jesus' teaching: love that goes lower — to servants, to strangers, to enemies.

verse.text: He got up from the meal, took off his outer clothing, and wrapped a towel around his waist.

blocks.text: The night before he is crucified, Jesus kneels and washes feet — the job reserved for the lowest servant. The King of the universe does the job nobody would do. Everything you will follow in the Jesus way is hidden in that towel: love expressed as descent.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do the literal equivalent: pick up the job no one should have to
Let yourself be served — the other half of washing feet
Check your heart's altitude: are you descending today?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus for the towel, the basin and the descent
Ask him to make your love walk downward

days.title: I have set you an example

verse.text: I have set you an example that you should do as I have done for you.

blocks.text: Jesus doesn't just warm our hearts with the gesture; he hands us the basin. Do as I have done. Love that goes lower is not a feeling to admire; it's an assignment. Put on the towel.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Serve someone who can never pay you back
Let your leadership be towel-led, not title-led
Ask: what does 'as I have done' mean in my actual day?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive his example as your assignment
Ask for joy in the descent — not just duty

verse.text: Love your neighbour as yourself.

blocks.text: The command is ordinary-sounding until you define neighbour. Jesus demolishes every border the word 'neighbour' usually draws. It is not whoever is easy or like you — it's whoever is in front of you, in need. Even the ones you'd rather cross the street to avoid.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let the definition of neighbour expand by one category today
Love one stranger with the energy you usually save for friends
Include yourself in 'as yourself' — that's the baseline, not the prize

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to redefine your neighbours
Thank him that he treated himself as ordinary love demands you be treated

verse.text: Just as I have loved you, you also should love one another.

blocks.text: Jesus upgrades the old command: love one another 'as I have loved you' — with the towel, the basin, the willingness to go low when it costs. A group of believers that loves like that is the most dangerous sign on earth.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Wash someone's feet — literally or figuratively — today
Choose the low seat at the gathering, not the important one
Protect the dignity of someone who's been brought low

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the grace to love as Jesus loved
Thank him for the new commandment that is not new at all

verse.text: But I tell you, love your enemies.

blocks.text: This is the hardest line in the sermon, and Jesus doesn't soften it. Love your enemies — the ones who've hurt you, opposed you, wronged your people. Today's quiz is about what loving an enemy does not mean.

blocks.question: What does 'love your enemies' NOT mean?
options: Pretending the hurt never happened
Praying for their good and refusing to repay evil with evil
blocks.explain: Right — loving enemies is not denial; it is a disciplined refusal to let them write your heart's programming.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Name an enemy to Jesus and pray for their good
Ask for power to break the cycle of repayment

verse.text: Go and do likewise.

blocks.text: The lawyer gets the story's final order: go and do likewise — be the neighbour, even to the person your society trains you to walk past. On a rest day, rest includes readiness: the story is always waiting to be re-enacted in your week.

blocks.prompt: Who is your 'roadside' person — the one your world steps around? Write how a towel-shaped love might meet them this month.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be the neighbour without borders
Thank Jesus for being the neighbour you didn't deserve

verse.text: This is how we know what love is: Jesus Christ laid down his life for us. And we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers and sisters.

blocks.text: Here is the definition and the reach of the lower love: he laid down his life; we lay down ours — daily, for real people, in real doses. Monday is the day to rehearse your own small death: a pride, a plan, a preference, laid down for someone.

blocks.prompt: What would 'laying down your life' concretely mean this month? Write one specific act and put it in your calendar.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Contemplate the love that laid down his life
Ask for strength to lay yours down in real doses

intro.text: The Jesus way is allergic to masks. This week we walk in the truth that sets free: honesty with God, honesty with ourselves, honesty with one another.

verse.text: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.

blocks.text: Truth is not a burden to survive here; it is the key. You will know the truth, and it will set you free. The most common bondage in the modern soul is not lack of information but lack of honesty — we lie to ourselves and wonder why we're stuck.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Tell one true thing to God today — the unedited version
Name the lie you've been privately rehearsing
Choose truth over the smoother story in one conversation

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the Spirit of truth to search your corners
Thank God that knowing the truth actually sets you free

verse.text: Instead, speaking the truth in love, we will grow to become in every respect the mature body of him who is the head, that is, Christ.

blocks.text: Truth without love is cruelty; love without truth is haze. Paul unites the two into one verb: speaking the truth in love — the way you grow up and the way the church grows up. One without the other just doesn't mature anything.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say one hard true thing — in love, not in frustration
Receive a hard true thing without building walls
Check your mix: is your kindness costing the truth?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for truth that travels in love
Thank God that he wants both, not either

verse.text: I am the way and the truth and the life.

blocks.text: Jesus doesn't just teach truth; he claims to be it. The way you walk this spring is a person, the truth you know is a person, the life you're given is a person. That changes everything about how you hold 'truth' — it is met, not just mastered.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Meet the truth today more than you measure it
Stop using truth as a weapon and start letting it set you free
Take one step on the way that is a person

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Worship Jesus as the way, the truth, the life
Ask him to be known, not just studied

verse.text: If we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another.

blocks.text: John's picture of honesty: walking in the light — things visible, nothing curated for the dark. The surprise is that this is where fellowship lives. Hidden things separate; shared things connect.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Bring one hidden thing into the light today
Offer someone your honest story, not your highlight reel
Enjoy the strange lightness of nothing to manage

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for courage to walk in the light
Thank God that his light covers, not exposes, those who come to him

verse.text: Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed.

blocks.text: James turns confession into a healing practice between people, not just a private transaction with God. Today's quiz is about the strange medicine of honest confession.

blocks.question: Why does James connect confession with healing?
options: Hidden sin keeps you sick; brought to light, it can be prayed over and healed
Confession is only for the faint-hearted
blocks.explain: Right — secrecy breeds infection; confession opens the wound to prayer and the balm of community.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray for the courage of honest confession
Ask for healing where secrets have made you sick

verse.text: Create in me a pure heart, O God.

blocks.text: David's post-failure prayer is the prayer of the honest soul: create in me a pure heart. He doesn't defend; he asks for reconstruction. On a rest day, let the truth do its work — the psalmists call it a clean heart, and it is the rest of the honest.

blocks.prompt: Write the prayer of a pure heart in your own words. What are you asking God to create in you?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Pray David's prayer for a pure heart
Trust that honesty with God is never the wrong door

verse.text: The LORD detests lying lips, but he delights in people who are trustworthy.

blocks.text: The way of truth ends where it began: a choice between two identities — the lying lips and the trustworthy heart. God delights in trustworthy people. On Monday, resolve to be one: true in the little things, and therefore true in the big ones.

blocks.prompt: Where are you tempted to trim the truth in small ways? Write the places — and your resolve for each.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be someone God delights in — trustworthy
Thank him for truth, the surgery that sets free

intro.text: Jesus talked about money more than almost anything because money is where the heart sets its real coordinates. This week we walk the way of the kingdom through the myth that you can't be spiritual and financial.

verse.text: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

blocks.text: Jesus doesn't say your heart directs your treasure; he says your treasure directs your heart. Your bank statement is a spiritual autobiography whether you intend it or not. The Jesus way starts with honesty about where the treasure is going.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do the uncomfortable audit: what do your spending patterns confess?
Move one unit of treasure toward Jesus' priorities today
Ask where your heart has actually been living

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Hand Jesus the ledger of your heart
Ask for hearts anchored where your treasure should be

verse.text: You cannot serve both God and money.

blocks.text: Jesus frames money as a rival god, not a tool. Money is not neutral; it is a loyalty that wants worship — security, status, control. The Jesus way dethrones it, not by pretending it doesn't exist but by refusing it the throne.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Worship-check: where did you look for safety today — God or money?
Practice a small act of financial risk-trust (give, lend, bless)
Refuse one fear-based decision led by money

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Reaffirm: serve God, not money
Ask for freedom from money's grip on your decisions

verse.text: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; do not trust your cleverness.

blocks.text: The proverb sounds cynical but is simply honest: money is a restless bird — it sprouts wings and flies off. Investing your life in the chasing of it is a treadmill with no exit. Wisdom refuses to be hypnotised by the flight of riches.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Refuse one 'get rich quick' thought today as a matter of principle
Invest in one thing that doesn't sprout wings: a person, a skill, the kingdom
Talk honestly with a friend about money — grieve the taboo

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for wisdom where money is concerned
Thank God that he is wealth that cannot flee

verse.text: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much.

blocks.text: Jesus teaches that money management is trust management. The way you handle the little (however little) is exactly how God tests what he can entrust to you. Faithfulness precedes favour.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Manage some 'little' with utter faithfulness today — time, a small sum, a duty
Ask: what would faithful stewardship look like if nothing was 'mine'?
Let integrity in money speak louder than your talk about it

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be trusted with little so you can be trusted with much
Thank God that he is the owner; you are the steward

verse.text: But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where moths and vermin do not destroy.

blocks.text: There is a bank that inflation, moths and market crashes can't touch: heaven. Today's quiz is about the wisdom of the two treasuries.

blocks.question: What is the practical test of where you're storing treasure?
options: How much you give away — treasure you can't keep anyway
How little you spend on yourself
blocks.explain: Right — heavenly treasure is a giving kind. The test is not austerity; it is direction.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask where your treasure is truly piling up
Thank God for a treasure that vermin cannot touch

verse.text: Come with me by yourselves to a quiet place and get some rest.

blocks.text: Even Jesus pulled his disciples out of the pace for a quiet rest. The kingdom is not fuelled by burnout. On a rest day, let the chassis cool — away from the metrics, the comparisons, the to-do list. Rest is not a reward; it's a royal entitlement.

blocks.prompt: Write down what rest actually looks like for you now — not a luxury plan, a real one. What would Jesus tell you to lay down today?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Come to the quiet place with Jesus
Thank him that rest is built into the kingdom's economy

verse.text: Remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.

blocks.text: Moses warns Israel, as they enter wealth: don't forget the Giver of the producing power. Every salary, salary-increase, opportunity and skill is downstream from God's giving. On Monday, steward the wealth — and remember where the ability came from.

blocks.prompt: What ability to produce have you been given? Treasure it this week — and give thanks for the Giver behind your game.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the ability to produce
Ask him to guard your heart from forgetting the Giver

intro.text: Prayer is not a slot in your schedule; it is the way you breathe on the Jesus way. This week we practise the kind of prayer Jesus taught — honest, persistent, trusting.

verse.text: This, then, is how you should pray: "Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name."

blocks.text: The model prayer begins with address, not agenda: our Father. Not 'my' — ours, a family prayer. Hevenly, hallowed. Before a single request, Jesus re-establishes who you are talking to: your Father, whose name you love.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Start prayer with address today: 'Our Father' — and mean it
Pray with someone else's need on your mind, not just yours
Slow down the opening: hallow his name before you ask anything

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Come to your Father as a family member
Ask that his name be revered in your life

verse.text: Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you.

blocks.text: Three verbs, one promise, and all of them are active. God is not inviting passive wishing; he is inviting persistent engagement — ask, seek, knock. The repetition is the point: the door opens to those who keep on coming.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Ask — out loud, specifically, for a real thing
Seek — take one actual search step toward your answer
Knock — don't give up after the first silence

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Bring your specific ask to your Father
Trust the promise: keep, seek, knock today

verse.text: Because this widow keeps bothering me, I will see that she gets justice.

blocks.text: Jesus tells a story of a widow who wears down a crooked judge — and then contrasts: if an unjust judge finally answers, how much more will a righteous Father? The point is not that God needs nagging; it's that persistence is the shape of faith.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Refuse to stop praying for one long-running thing
Let the widow's stubbornness be your model, not your embarrassment
Ask yourself: have I really persisted, or given up quietly?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Lay your one persistent request before the righteous judge
Thank him that he is not a grudging judge but a Father

verse.text: In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. We do not know what we ought to pray for, but the Spirit himself intercedes for us.

blocks.text: There is enormous relief in this verse: you don't always know what to pray. When words fail, the Spirit prays in you with groans deeper than language. Prayer is not a performance art; it is a partnership.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give voice to a prayer you can't articulate — let the Spirit interpret
Admit your weakness in prayer out loud — it's the Spirit's cue
Pray through silence sometimes; groans count

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let the Spirit pray in your weakness today
Thank him that he intercedes when you can't find words

verse.text: He withdrew... and prayed.

blocks.text: The busiest man in the gospels kept withdrawing to pray. Jesus' rhythm of life was built on it — not prayer squeezed around a full schedule but the schedule built on prayer. Today's quiz is about Jesus' prayer practice.

blocks.question: What pattern did Jesus model in his busiest seasons?
options: Cutting prayer because the demands were urgent
Withdrawing to pray before and during the demands
blocks.explain: Right — Jesus made withdrawal to pray, not the workload, the foundation of his priorities.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Withdraw deliberately to pray
Follow Jesus into the quiet before the demands

verse.text: My soul finds rest in God alone.

blocks.text: Prayer is not only petition; it is resting your soul in God like a patient on a table. On a rest day, let prayer be less about raising hands with requests and more about letting go of everything you were gripping.

blocks.prompt: Sit in stillness for five minutes. What does your soul say when it isn't performing? Write two sentences.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest your soul in God alone
Thank him that prayer's deepest posture is trust

verse.text: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, faithful in prayer.

blocks.text: Paul's triple rhythm runs on the third rail: faithful in prayer. It is the current that keeps joy from curdling and patience from snapping. Monday is the day to wire prayer into your week like a power cable, not an ornament.

blocks.prompt: Write your practical prayer plan for the week: when, where, and the one thing you will persist on.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Commit to faithfulness in prayer this week
Thank God that the Spirit is in it with you

intro.text: Halfway through spring we walk to the centre: the cross. The Jesus way runs through it — not as decoration but as the shape of a surrendered life.

verse.text: Whoever wants to be my disciple must deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.

blocks.text: In Jesus' world a cross was one thing — an instrument of execution, carried by a condemned man to his own death. He invites followers to the same posture: deny yourself, take it up, follow. The way of Jesus is a death-sentence life and the only one worth living.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one self-centred default you can deny today
Pick up the daily cross: the obedience you'd rather avoid
Follow — not negotiate — today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the invitation to the cross-shaped life
Ask for the grace to deny yourself and follow

verse.text: Yet not as I will, but as you will.

blocks.text: In Gethsemane Jesus prays the most honest prayer ever prayed: Father, if it's possible, take this cup — and then, not as I will but as you will. The cross-shaped life is not the absence of preference; it is preference surrendered.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Say honestly to God what you'd prefer — then surrender it
Practise the two-clause prayer: my will, then yours
Let surrender be a daily rhythm, not a one-time event

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Bring your honest preference to the Father
End every prayer where Jesus ended his: not my will, but yours

verse.text: He humbled himself by becoming obedient to death — even death on a cross!

blocks.text: Paul gives the descent its full depth: Jesus did not merely serve or teach or wash feet — he humbled himself to death, even death on a cross. The cross is the bottom of the descent, and it is where the way of Jesus is measured. How low will love go?

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Trade a right you're entitled to for the sake of another today
Study the cross and let it reset your ambitions
Serve someone as if humility were still trending

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Contemplate the humility that went to the cross
Ask for the same mind that was in Christ Jesus

verse.text: When he had received the drink, Jesus said, "It is finished."

blocks.text: The cross is where striving ends. It is finished — the debt paid, the work completed, the verdict rendered. The cross-shaped life is not 'try harder to be saved'; it is 'already saved, now live it'. Your performance on the way is love's response, not the wage.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Stop earning what is already finished
Live today as someone already forgiven — light, not striving
Let the finished work end one of your self-condemnation loops

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive the finished work of the cross
Thank Jesus that the debt is paid in full

verse.text: I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me.

blocks.text: Paul's audacious claim: the old life is dead, executed with Jesus; what lives now is Christ in him. Today's quiz tests which 'I' died at the cross.

blocks.question: According to Galatians 2:20, what died with Christ?
options: The old self that lived for itself
The desire to ever experience difficulty
blocks.explain: Right — 'I have been crucified with Christ': the old ruler, the self-life, was executed. The life that remains is Christ's in you.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rehearse the exchange: dead to self, alive to Christ
Ask Christ to live so evidently in you

verse.text: Later, knowing that everything had now been finished, and so that Scripture would be fulfilled, Jesus said, "I am thirsty."

blocks.text: Even his thirst was completion. On a rest day, let the cross do its quiet work: every burden you carry about your worth, your standing, your failures — finished. Rest is not earned at the foot of this cross; it is received.

blocks.prompt: What are you still trying to 'finish' that Jesus already declared finished? Write it down — then receive it as finished.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest at the foot of the finished cross
Thank Jesus that every 'it is finished' is for you

verse.text: May I never boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

blocks.text: The cross-shaped life has one boast: the cross. Not your resume, your church attendance, your moral record — but the executed Son and his finished grace. On Monday, choose your boast and let it reorder the week.

blocks.prompt: What have you been quietly boasting in? Swap it today for the only boast that holds — write the swap down.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Boast in the cross of Christ alone today
Thank him for the humility that funds your salvation

weeks.title: Week 8 — Faith for the long road

intro.text: Spring faith is easy; the long road of a lifetime is where it's tested. This week we walk the endurance of faith — waiting, hoping, not giving up, keeping first things first.

verse.text: Now faith is confidence in what we hope for and assurance about what we do not see.

blocks.text: The long road runs on two rails: confidence in what is hoped for, assurance about what is not yet seen. Faith is not certainty about details; it is settled trust in the Character behind the promises. That trust is the road beneath your feet.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name what you hope for — confidently, not wishfully
Hold assurance for what you cannot yet see
Choose trust in the Character, not certainty on the details

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the confidence of faith today
Thank God for being trustworthy on the unseen road

verse.text: If you have faith as small as a mustard seed... Nothing will be impossible for you.

blocks.text: The disciples ask why they couldn't drive out the demon, and Jesus points to the tiny seed: faith the size of a mustard seed. Faith is not about magnitude; it's about placement — a small amount resting fully on a large God.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Bring your small, honest faith — not a pretend big one
Stop measuring faith by feelings and start by obedience
Act on the seed you have; it's enough

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Present your mustard seed to the God of the impossible
Thank him that he works with small and honest faith

verse.text: Let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us.

blocks.text: The long road is a race 'marked out for us' — not a race we choose, but the one appointed. And it is run with perseverance: the unglamorous stamina of showing up again. The witnesses in the stands (the previous chapter's hall of faith) know how it ends.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Receive your marked-out race without resentful comparisons
Define success as persistence, not position
Run today's lap — you don't have to run tomorrow's

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for perseverance, the gift of the long haul
Thank God for the cloud of witnesses rooting you on

verse.text: Fixing our eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of faith.

blocks.text: The antidote to giving up: fixed eyes. Not on the difficulty, not even on your faith, but on Jesus — the pioneer who went first and the perfecter who completes what he started. The road holds because the eyes hold.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: When the road feels endless, return your eyes to Jesus
Follow the pioneer: he has walked every stretch before you
Trust the perfecter: he finishes what he starts

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Fix your eyes on the pioneer and perfecter
Thank Jesus for going first and finishing last

verse.text: Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off everything that hinders.

blocks.text: You are not the first, or the last. Hebrews 11 lists the long-distance runners of faith — Abraham, Moses, Rahab — and says they surround you like a stadium. Today's quiz is on where a long-distance runner gets their assurance.

blocks.question: What let the heroes of faith endure the unseen road?
options: Seeing their reward in the crowd's approval
Seeing him who is invisible, and trusting the promise
blocks.explain: Right — Hebrews says Moses 'persevered because he saw him who is invisible'. Assurance is about the unseen God, not the visible crowd.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Honour the witnesses who have run before you
Ask for strength to follow their footsteps home

verse.text: In repentance and rest is your salvation, in quietness and trust is your strength.

blocks.text: The long road has a built-in pace: rest. Isaiah calls it quietness and trust — not the exhaustion of speed but the staying-power of rest in God. On a rest day, receive the gift that rescues you from burnout's slow sabotage.

blocks.prompt: Where have you been running on fumes? Write where rest — real rest — needs to re-enter your weekly rhythm.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Receive quietness and trust as your strength
Thank God that rest is the pace of the long road

verse.text: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.

blocks.text: Paul ends his life with the threefold finish-line report: fought the good fight, finished the race, kept the faith. Not 'won every round' but 'kept the faith'. Monday is for making peace with the race being long and the finish being faithful, not flawless.

blocks.prompt: Write what 'kept the faith' would look like at the end of your life. What does that change about this week?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the grace to finish faithful
Thank God for the crown that waits for those who love his appearing

intro.text: Unforgiveness is a weight that grows in the dark. This week we walk the hardest freedom in the kingdom: forgiveness without limit — for the family, the church, and the people who have hurt you most.

verse.text: I tell you, not seven times, but seventy-seven times.

blocks.text: Peter offers his ceiling — seven times, generous by any standard — and Jesus explodes the counting: seventy-seven. The point is not arithmetic but disposition: stop keeping the books. Unforgiveness always starts bookkeeping; forgiveness starts ledger-burning.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find a tally you've been keeping and burn it
Forgive a person again for the same offence — that's the seventy-seven way
Ask: who am I still 'not' forgiving?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the grace to stop counting
Thank God whose forgiveness already tore up your ledger

verse.text: Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
