blocks.text: An anchor holds a boat through storms without the boat seeing what's holding it. That's hope: an anchor for your soul. When your feelings wave around — and they will — the anchor holds. Hope is not guessing things will be fine; it's a settled trust in Someone who has proven Himself firm and secure.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Watch a rope or string hold something steady
Name one storm your hope is currently holding
Tell God: 'my hope's anchor is You'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to hold your soul steady when feelings wave
Thank Him for a hope that is firm and secure

verse.text: Truly he is my rock and my salvation; he is my fortress, I will not be shaken.

blocks.text: The psalmist stacks words like stones: rock, salvation, fortress. Notice the end of the line — 'I will not be shaken.' Not 'He will not shake' but 'I will not be shaken,' because standing on something unshakable changes what you are. The unmoved rock makes the mover stand still.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Stand on something solid and feel the difference
Repeat three times: 'He is my rock, I will not be shaken'
Name one thing that used to shake you — is it smaller now?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Stand on the rock and feel stable
Thank God your fortress is not made of feelings

verse.text: Everyone who hears these words of mine and puts them into practice is like a wise man who built his house on the rock.

blocks.text: Quiz day on foundations. The wise builder and the foolish builder heard the same words — the difference was the digging. It's not about who knows Scripture; it's about who digs down and obeys. Ready to check your taproot?

blocks.question: In Jesus' story, what made the wise man's house stand through the storm?
options: He used the best brick and the most expensive wood
He dug down deep and laid his foundation on rock
He built somewhere high that the water couldn't reach
He kept his house very small
blocks.explain: The hearer who puts Jesus' words into practice is like the man who dug down deep and laid his foundation on rock (Matthew 7:24-25). The difference was not the house; it was the depth.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to help you dig deeper this week
Thank Him that He is the rock under it all

verse.text: He makes me lie down in green pastures, he leads me beside quiet waters, he refreshes my soul.

blocks.text: The Shepherd makes us lie down. Sheep have to be laid down — they won't rest on their own, they get anxious and graze wildly. God, the perfect Shepherd, sometimes has to 'make' you rest. Day 6 is His green pasture. Let yourself be led out of the hurry and refreshed.

blocks.prompt: When did your soul last get 'refreshed' — truly restored, not just distracted? What would a green-pasture day look like this week?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the Shepherd to make you lie down
Thank Him for quiet waters just for you

verse.text: If you continue in your faith, established and firm, and do not move from the hope held out in the gospel.

blocks.text: Taproots are made by continuing. One good day doesn't make a deep root; months of small, boring, faithful days do. This week you anchored a lot of truth. Now the anchor works like any anchor — by staying. End the week firm and standing.

blocks.prompt: Which single truth from this week do you want to keep standing on? Write it where you'll see it.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to establish what He began this week
Thank Him for a rock, not sand, under your feet

intro.text: Now we test the roots. Not every season is gentle growth — some weeks the wind comes. Storms are how you find out what your taproot is really anchored to.

verse.text: They are like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid the foundation on rock. When a flood came, the torrent struck that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.

blocks.text: Notice the order in this verse. The man dug first, and the flood came later. Nobody builds a foundation in the middle of a flood. The storms that are hitting your life right now — or the ones coming next month — are the reason today's quiet digging matters. What feels like a boring Tuesday is actually building your storm-proofing.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one storm you're facing now or expecting soon
Ask: what depth is that storm going to test in me?
Do one boring, good habit today — that's your digging

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to dig you deeper before the storm arrives
Thank Him that storms reveal, they don't defeat

verse.text: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear, though the earth give way.

blocks.text: 'Therefore we will not fear' — and then the extreme cases: earth giving way, mountains falling into the sea. The psalmist isn't imagining a tiny storm; he's imagining the end of the world, and still refusing fear. Why? Because 'God is our refuge' comes before 'therefore.' The reason precedes the fearlessness. Know the reason first.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Write the word 'therefore' and what comes before it
Name one 'earth giving way' fear you can hand to God
Say: 'God is ever-present help in this trouble'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Tell God the extreme-case fears you're carrying
Ask Him to be your refuge before the wind rises

verse.text: He got up, rebuked the wind and said to the waves, 'Quiet! Be still!' Then the wind died down and it was completely calm.

blocks.text: The disciples panicked with Jesus asleep in their own boat. He was right there, and they still thought they were sinking alone. The storm was real, but so was the passenger. When your world is loud, remember who is in the boat with you. He can say 'Be still' to things you can't even see yet.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name the 'storm' that feels loudest right now
Remind yourself: Jesus is in this same boat
Tell Him: 'You're allowed to wake up for this one'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to speak peace into your loudest storm
Thank Him that He rides the boat with you

verse.text: Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand.

blocks.text: Notice the goal of the armor: not to win the whole battle, not to be invincible — to stand. 'After you have done everything, to stand.' Storms don't ask you to be impressive; they ask you to not fall over. Some days, standing up straight with your armor on is the entire victory. Roots win by holding.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Stand up straight right now — posture isn't just physical
Put on one piece of God's armor mentally for the day
Set your goal as 'stand today,' not 'fix everything today'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to armor you for the day of evil
Thank Him that standing still counts as winning

verse.text: But everyone who hears these words of mine and does not put them into practice is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.

blocks.text: Storms don't punish the foolish; they expose the sand. The foolish man may have had a nicer view. But both builders got the same rain — and only one root was tested. Take the storm quiz and get your foundation checked.

blocks.question: Why did the foolish builder's house fall in the storm?
options: His storm was stronger than the wise man's storm
He put his house on sand instead of rock
He didn't hear Jesus' words at all
He hurried and used cheap materials
blocks.explain: Both builders heard Jesus' words; the difference was doing them. The foolish man 'built his house on sand' (Matthew 7:26) — no deep dig, no rock, and the storm exposed it.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to find any patch of sand in your foundation
Thank Him for the rock even while the rain falls

verse.text: But I have calmed and quieted myself, I am like a weaned child with its mother; like a weaned child I am content.

blocks.text: A weaned child next to its mother isn't fussing for milk anymore — it just rests in her. That's the picture of storm-settled trust: not 'God, where's my answer?' but 'God, I'm with You and I'm content.' Rest day: quiet yourself like that. Let the storm shout; you've already decided who's with you.

blocks.prompt: When you're in the middle of a storm, what steadies you the fastest? What 'quieting' is God teaching you?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Calm and quiet yourself before God
Thank Him for being enough even without the answer yet

verse.text: The Lord is good, a refuge in times of trouble. He cares for those who trust in him.

blocks.text: A week of storms, and we end with a small, fierce verse: the Lord is good, a refuge in times of trouble. Not a storehouse in times of ease — a refuge in trouble. That's when He shows up best. Write the verse somewhere, name the storm, and put your name where 'those who trust in him' goes.

blocks.prompt: Looking back at this week, where did you feel God's protection in the middle of trouble?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for being good even when it's stormy
Ask Him to keep being your refuge next week

intro.text: Here is a gardener's secret you may not like at first: the best trees get cut. Pruning hurts for a season and grows the tree for years. This week we learn to trust the Gardener's knife.

verse.text: He cuts off every branch in me that bears no fruit, while every branch that does bear fruit he prunes so that it will be even more fruitful.

blocks.text: There are two kinds of cutting in this verse, but they don't scare either kind of branch. The dead branch gets removed; the healthy branch gets pruned — clipped back so the tree's energy goes to fruit instead of to everywhere at once. Getting pruned isn't punishment. It means the Gardener believes you can bear more fruit.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Pick a habit that spreads you thin — the Gardener might clip it
Name one thing God has 'cut back' that later helped you
Thank God that pruning means He expects fruit

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Tell the Gardener He may cut what needs cutting
Thank Him that He prunes what bears fruit

verse.text: No discipline seems pleasant at the time, but painful. Later on, however, it produces a harvest of righteousness and peace.

blocks.text: God is honest about it: discipline doesn't feel pleasant at the time. Anyone who says growing is always easy is not a gardener. But then comes the 'however' — the pivot. Later, it produces a harvest. You can't taste the harvest on pruning day. That's why we tell each other the truth about it now.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Think of one 'however' God is growing in your life
Be honest with God about the part that feels painful
Say: 'I will judge this season by its harvest, not its cuts'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for the 'however' — patience for the harvest
Tell Him the honest truth about what the cut feels like

verse.text: Create in me a pure heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.

blocks.text: David sang this after being exposed — after the pruning had to be severe. The word he uses is 'create': God, make a new heart in me, not just patch the old one. Pruning that removes sin is an act of creation. What looks like loss at the branch is actually blessing at the root. Let God have the branches He is reaching for.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let God show you one 'branch' that needs to go
Ask Him to create, not just patch
Say with David: 'renew a steadfast spirit in me'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God for a created-clean heart
Thank Him that He cuts, then creates

verse.text: Because the Lord disciplines those he loves, as a father the son he delights in.

blocks.text: The deepest truth about pruning is this: it comes from love. A gardener who prunes cares whether the tree fruits. A stranger doesn't bother. When God's direction cuts into your plans, it's not rejection — it's the classic parent move: because I delight in you, I'm not leaving you to grow wild.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Reframe one hard 'correction' as God's delight in you
Watch a real parent or gardener tend something carefully
Say out loud: 'God disciplines the ones He loves'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that His cuts come from His delight
Ask Him to correct you like a father who loves you

verse.text: This is to my Father's glory, that you bear much fruit, showing yourselves to be my disciples.

blocks.text: Quiz day — and the key question is what all this pruning is for. It's not so your branch looks impressive. It's that you bear much fruit, and fruit brings glory to the Father, not the branch. The branch that is clipped the most often bears the most. Let's check what you remember about the Gardener's work.

blocks.question: What does the Father prune a branch that already bears fruit?
options: To punish it for growing too well
So it will be even more fruitful
To keep it small enough to manage
So other branches can get more sun
blocks.explain: John 15:2: 'every branch that does bear fruit he prunes so that it will be even more fruitful.' Pruning is a promotion, not a punishment — more fruit is the goal.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to bear fruit that brings the Father glory
Thank Him that He prunes branches He plans to use

verse.text: I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go; I will counsel you with my loving eye on you.

blocks.text: Rest day after a week of pruning. The beautiful thing about being taught and counseled is that you're not left bleeding at the cut — you're guided. 'I will counsel you with my loving eye on you.' The Gardener who pruned is now watching over the healing. Rest in that.

blocks.prompt: What is God currently 'teaching you in the way you should go'? What direction does this pruning season seem to be pointing?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let God counsel you with His loving eye
Thank Him that pruning isn't the end — teaching is

verse.text: Let us throw off everything that hinders and the sin that so easily entangles. And let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us.

blocks.text: Pruning is a runner's weight cut. The verse calls it throwing off what hinders — things that aren't even sin, just weight. Not every cut removes sin; some cuts free your energy. End the week by asking: what did you drop, and what can you now run faster for?

blocks.prompt: What is the heaviest thing you're carrying that isn't sin, just weight? What would 'throwing it off' look like?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to show you what hinders you
Thank Him for a lighter, faster season ahead

intro.text: A pruned branch is still attached to the tree. This week we zoom in on the oneness — the trunk, the vine, the one body we all grow from. Nobody grows alone; everybody is attached to somebody.

verse.text: Remain in me, as I also remain in you. No branch can bear fruit by itself; it must remain in the vine. Neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in me.

blocks.text: A branch doesn't 'try harder' to bear fruit. It stays attached. Fruit happens when a branch simply remains connected to the vine that feeds it. The Christian life at its most mature is not a frenzy — it's a remaining. Stay connected, and fruit comes by itself, like it does for apple branches.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Check your connection before you check your output
Do one 'remaining' habit: pray, read, sit with God
Trust that connection, not effort, produces fruit

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to help you remain, not strive
Thank Him that fruit comes from connection

verse.text: Just as a body, though one, has many parts, but all its many parts form one body, so it is with Christ.

blocks.text: The trunk sends the same sap to every branch, but not every branch is on the same side of the tree. Some face east, some face west; some are high, some are low. Your part of God's family looks different from the church down the street — that's not division, that's a body. Different parts, one body, same sap.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Spot a way your church differs from another — celebrate it
Use one talent or 'part' of you to serve someone
Say: 'many parts, one body, same sap'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for being One over many parts
Ask how to use your part to serve the body

verse.text: So in Christ we, though many, form one body, and each member belongs to all the others.

blocks.text: Here's the best part of the one-body teaching: 'each member belongs to all the others.' You don't just attend church; you belong to people. When a branch on the far side of the tree is hurt, the whole tree feels it. Belonging means someone's joy is your joy, someone's storm is your storm.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name the three people you 'belong to'
Do something that shares someone's joy or lightens their load
Tell one person: 'you belong to us'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that you belong to a body
Ask to carry one person's storm this week

verse.text: If some of the branches have been broken off, and you, though a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others and now share in the nourishing sap from the olive root.

blocks.text: Here's the wildest garden fact in the Bible: some of you weren't born on this tree. You're a wild olive shoot — grafted in. Nothing about you was native. The tree's root reaches all the way to God's promises, and now you share the sap. You didn't earn the trunk. You received the trunk. That changes how kind you are to the other branches.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Remind yourself: you were grafted in, not born attached
Show a new person the welcome you received
Say: 'I share the sap of God's promises'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for grafting you into His tree
Ask to be as welcoming as the graft you received

verse.text: I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing.

blocks.text: Quiz day on the most important attachment in your life. Jesus takes the picture from the grapevine — the branch that looks great but is clipped from the vine withers fast. Remember: the branch's whole future is the attachment. Here's your check: do you know exactly what grows you?

blocks.question: Jesus said 'apart from me you can do ____.' What's the complete ending?
options: a few things, if you try hard
nothing
everything, eventually
better than when you're attached
blocks.explain: John 15:5: 'apart from me you can do nothing.' The branch disconnected from the vine might look fine for an hour, but fruit is impossible without the attachment.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus that He is the vine holding you
Ask to stay attached and let fruit come

verse.text: How good and pleasant it is when God's people live together in unity!

blocks.text: Rest day — and this week's rest is about people. 'How good and pleasant' — the psalmist almost tastes it. Unity isn't a management goal; it's pleasant, life-giving, like oil on your head or dew on the mountain. Spend today with people you belong to, and let it feel as good as it's meant to.

blocks.prompt: Who are you most grateful to belong to? What does their 'sap' look like in your life — how do they feed you?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the people who carry His sap to you
Ask to be pleasant unity, not a knot

verse.text: Make every effort to keep the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace.

blocks.text: Unity is worth effort, and the verse says exactly how: through peace. Not through being right all the time or winning debates — through the bond of peace. A tree doesn't snap at its own branches. End the week with one commitment: the branch on your left and the branch on your right, peace you will keep.

blocks.prompt: Is there a branch in your tree you need to make peace with this week? Name it honestly.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to keep you unified through peace
Thank Him for the trunk that holds all of you together

intro.text: Attached branches grow outward. This week we talk about reaching — the branches of your life moving toward other people, as service and as shelter.

verse.text: Enlarge the place of your tent, stretch your tent curtains wide, do not hold back; lengthen your cords, strengthen your stakes.

blocks.text: This is a stretching verse. It assumes your tent is too small and your welcome is too narrow. Lengthen the cords, strengthen the stakes — a bigger tent needs stronger anchoring. The way you grow outward is by going deeper. That's why we spent seven weeks on roots before we asked you to reach anyone.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find one person who is outside your 'tent'
Do one thing that makes your welcome wider
Check your stakes: is your inner root strong enough for this?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to widen your life without shallowizing it
Thank Him for tents meant to be expanded

verse.text: Carry each other's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.

blocks.text: Branches carry more than their own leaves. A good branch holds up the branch next to it in heavy fruit. 'Carry each other's burdens' — that's not a metaphor for advice-giving. It means literally taking weight off someone: carrying the scolding voice in your head for them, carrying the load so they can breathe. Christ's whole law, fulfilled in the shape of a yield.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find one burden someone is carrying and carry part
Don't just advise — actually lift something
Notice who is carrying you, and thank them

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to show you a burden He wants you to share
Thank Him for the branch-holders in your life

verse.text: Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.

blocks.text: Every branch has an open latch, and Jesus' latch reads: 'Come to me, all you who are weary.' Before you can carry anyone else's burden, you have to know the rest He gives for your own. You're not the tree; you're a branch. Point the weary to the trunk that never gets tired.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Bring your own weariness to Jesus first
Receive His rest before you serve
Tell someone weary: 'come to Him'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Come to Jesus with your tired self
Ask Him to make you rest, then branch

verse.text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for a time of adversity.

blocks.text: Branch-shelter is what friendship is for. Fair-weather branches wave in fun and vanish in storms, but a friend loves 'at all times' — and the brother you're born for is meant for the hard time. Adversity doesn't test whether you're a nice person; it reveals whether you're a real branch to lean on.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Show a friend you love them on an ordinary day
Tell them: 'I'm here for your hard times too'
Thank one person who was born for your adversity

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for friends who are born for your storms
Ask to be that friend to someone

verse.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.

blocks.text: Quiz day — and this is the quiz about the whole direction of your life. The strongest branch of all didn't use its place to be served; the Son of Man came to serve. When you understand that, 'spreading branches' stops being a chore and becomes the shape of everything. Check what you remember.

blocks.question: The Son of Man came into the world to be ______. What belongs in the blank?
options: served
admired
serving
famous
blocks.explain: Mark 10:45: 'the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.' True greatness in God's tree faces outward.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask Jesus to shape you into a servant
Thank Him that He served, not so we could relax — so we could follow

verse.text: Keep me as the apple of your eye; hide me in the shadow of your wings.

blocks.text: Branches give shelter — and we also need shelter. Rest day. The same God who sends you to stretch your tent wide also hides you in the shadow of His wings. It's not selfish to be hidden for a day. Even a tree rests under the sky that covers it. Be the apple of His eye; rest there.

blocks.prompt: When have you most needed to be 'hidden'? What does shelter feel like in your life right now?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Hide in the shadow of His wings today
Thank Him that both sending and sheltering are His work

verse.text: Each of you should use whatever gift you have received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God's grace in its various forms.

blocks.text: Branches exists partly so birds can nest in them. Your gifts — your actual, particular talents and grace — are God's way of building nests. 'Whatever gift you have received, use it to serve others.' Nothing you're good at is wasted. The circut board you can fix, the joke you can tell, the quiet way you listen — all nest wood.

blocks.prompt: What gifts have you been given? Who might be able to 'nest' in them? List one concrete way to use one gift this week.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to show you the nests He wants built
Thank Him for gift-shaped grace, in its various forms

intro.text: A tree that bears fruit is meant to give it away. This week we get open-handed: generosity, sowing, and the strange math of God, where giving makes you richer.

verse.text: Each of you should give what you have decided in your heart to give, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.

blocks.text: Notice who loves what: God doesn't just accept your giving; He loves a cheerful giver. That means the heart of giving matters to Him as much as the amount. Money, time, snacks, forgiveness, attention — give what you've decided in your heart. A happy handful scatters better than a sulking trunkful.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give something with joy on purpose, not out of guilt
Notice the difference in how it feels
Ask God what HE wants you to decide in your heart

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make you a cheerful giver
Thank Him that He loves the joy in your giving

verse.text: Sow your seed in the morning, and at evening let your hands not be idle, for you do not know which will succeed, whether this or that, or whether both will do equally well.

blocks.text: The farmer sows without knowing which seed will make it — so he sows in the morning and doesn't slack in the evening. You don't know which kindness will land, which verse will stick, which prayer will be answered. So scatter. Generosity hedges against the mystery; the more you sow, the more of your life is in the ground growing.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Sow something small in the morning
Sow something (even tiny) in the evening
Don't track which one 'works' — just trust the farmer's math

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He knows which seeds will succeed
Ask for hands that stay open all day

verse.text: One person gives freely, yet gains even more; another withholds unduly, but comes to poverty.

blocks.text: This verse breaks your calculator. Freely given, gains more; tightly held, comes to poverty. It's the law of the harvest, and it holds for non-money things too. Grip your time and no one can use it; give it and it multiplies in memory and friendship. The tight fist was never the safe place.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Let go of one thing you've been gripping (time, credit, control)
Watch what it does when it's free
Say: 'open hands grow; tight fists shrink'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to uncurl your fingers
Thank Him for a kingdom where giving multiplies

verse.text: They all gave out of their wealth; but she, out of her poverty, put in everything — all she had to live on.

blocks.text: Jesus watched people give and quietly declared the poor widow the biggest giver of them all. Not because of the amount but because of what was left. She gave 'everything — all she had to live on.' God measures what remains, not just what's offered. Small seeds from a trusting hand is exactly how the kingdom is funded.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give something that actually costs you
Let it be 'everything' for your situation, even if tiny
Remember God weighs what's left behind

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the widow's kind of trust
Thank God that He counts sacrifice, not size

verse.text: Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.

blocks.text: Quiz day on the farmer's patience. The hardest part of sowing is that nothing shows for a while — and the verse warns against the exact failure: weariness, giving up. Take the quiz, then in your prayer, ask for the patience part.

blocks.question: Galatians 6:9 promises a harvest 'at the proper time' if we do what?
options: If we do not give up
If we give the most money
If we sow with the fastest-growing seeds
If we tell everyone about our sowing
blocks.explain: 'Let us not become weary in doing good, for at the proper time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up.' The harvest is guaranteed — the requirement is perseverance.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for perseverance in the invisible season
Thank God that reaping time is set, not guessed

verse.text: The Lord will indeed give what is good, and our land will yield its harvest.

blocks.text: Rest day from sowing. The land doesn't yield its harvest because you managed it perfectly — the Lord gives what is good. You scatter, and He grows. Today you don't have to be productive. Let the Lord do His part while your hands stay in your lap.

blocks.prompt: What is the one seed you most want to see grow this season? What would 'waiting at the proper time' feel like?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest while the Lord gives what is good
Thank Him for harvests you can't see yet

verse.text: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the Lord, and he will reward them for what they have done.

blocks.text: End the week with the most generous thought of all: when you're kind to someone with little, you're making a loan — to the Lord. Not a donation to a stranger; a loan to the King. There is no safer investment. Write your week-9 reflection as someone who has already deposited with God.

blocks.prompt: What did this week's generosity teach you about the 'strange math' of giving? What did you leave with open hands?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He receives kindness as a loan to Him
Ask to be a person whose hands stayed open all week

intro.text: Sowing is done; now we check the fruit. If roots send up anything, it's fruit — the visible character of your life. This week, we taste it.

verse.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

blocks.text: Here's the list: nine fruit, all growing from one Spirit. Not nine skills you must master — one orchard from one tree. And the strange final phrase: 'against such things there is no law.' You can never have too much of these. No rule was ever broken by too much kindness or gentleness.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Pick the two fruit your branch needs most this week
Ask the Spirit for one of them — not your own effort
Notice fruit on someone else's branch and tell them

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask the Spirit to grow the whole fruit list in you
Thank Him there is no law against too much fruit

verse.text: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.

blocks.text: Paul unpacks love so it's not a feeling but a behavior. Patient and kind are things you do. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud — things you refuse to do. Fruit you can test: today, was I patient? Was I kind? Did I envy or brag? Love shows up in verbs.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Do patience out loud today — wait without grumbling
Do kindness on purpose — one visible, small act
Catch yourself boasting once, and let it drop

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make His love into verbs in you
Thank Him that love can be practiced, not just felt

verse.text: Therefore, as God's chosen people, holy and dearly loved, clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness and patience.

blocks.text: Clothing is a choice you make daily — you pick what to put on. Paul says: as chosen, holy, dearly loved people, get dressed in compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, patience. It's a wardrobe. Some mornings you'll feel grumpy and want the old outfit. Choose the fruit anyway; it's how the dearly loved dress.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Get dressed in one fruit when you wake up
If the old grumpy outfit wins, change at lunch
Remember whose wardrobe it is — you're dearly loved

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to help you get dressed in His clothes
Thank Him that you're chosen, holy, and dearly loved

verse.text: For it is God who works in you to will and to act in order to fulfill his good purpose.

blocks.text: Who grows the fruit? It is God who works in you. Not 'work up fruit in yourself,' but 'it is God who works in you.' Both the wanting and the doing come from Him working inside. Your part is staying connected and saying yes. The Gardener does the growing.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: When you want to do good, thank God for the want
When you do good, thank God for the power
Rest in 'it is God who works in you'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He is working in you right now
Ask Him to fulfill His good purpose through your fruit

verse.text: For each tree is recognized by its own fruit.

blocks.text: Quiz day on identification. You can't always tell a tree by its bark or its leaves — but fruit doesn't lie. Fig trees are known by figs. People are known by patience, kindness, humility. Time to check: when people meet you, what fruit are they tasting?

blocks.question: How is a tree recognized, according to Luke 6:44?
options: By its height
By its own fruit
By its age
By how many leaves it drops
blocks.explain: Luke 6:44: 'For each tree is recognized by its own fruit.' You can guess by bark and leaves, but fruit is the honest identification — and so it is for people.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to grow fruit that identifies you well
Thank Him that He sees you as a tree, not a photo

verse.text: Then, because so many people were coming and going that they did not even have a chance to eat, he said to them, 'Come with me by yourselves to a quiet place and get some rest.'

blocks.text: Even Jesus' own disciples got so busy they didn't have time to eat — and Jesus' answer wasn't 'do more.' It was 'come with me by yourselves to a quiet place and get some rest.' Fruit-bearing trees need rest from people. Rest day: come away, by yourself, quiet. Go.

blocks.prompt: What fills your week so full there's 'no chance to eat'? What would a quiet place with Jesus actually look like for you?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Come away with Jesus to a quiet place
Thank Him that rest is a command, not a reward

verse.text: By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.

blocks.text: Jesus made fruit very simple and very enormous: the way everyone will know you're His disciple is love. Not the perfect doctrine quiz. Love one another. Week 10 closes with the whole orchard in one line. Finish your reflection, and let love be the fruit the season is remembered by.

blocks.prompt: Which fruit of the Spirit did you taste most this week? Which one is God reaching to grow in you next?
blocks.placeholder: God grew _____ in me this week

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to be known by love
Thank Jesus for a simple, enormous way to be recognized

intro.text: Put every picture together now: a tree planted right beside a river, roots reaching the stream, leaves green through the worst drought. This is the whole goal of the season — to live your life planted by living water.

verse.text: That person is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season and whose leaf does not wither — whatever they do prospers.

blocks.text: Psalm 1 gives us the fountainhead image of the whole season. Notice what the tree does NOT do: panic. It yields fruit in season — not in every season, but in season. It withers in no season. 'Whatever they do prospers' — not because nothing goes wrong, but because the water keeps coming and the roots stay connected.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Draw or imagine your tree planted by a river
Underline: 'fruit IN SEASON, no withering'
Name one thing that shouldn't wither in your life

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for streams that never dry
Ask to be planted, not just passing by

verse.text: They will be like a tree planted by the water that sends out its roots by the stream. It does not fear when heat comes; its leaves are always green.

blocks.text: The key phrase is 'does not fear when heat comes.' Tree-people don't deny the heat; they don't feel it the same way. The drought is real, but their supply line goes to the stream. Your anchor is what heats fear out of the picture. Read the verse again and put your own heat in the sentence.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name the 'heat' (pressure, deadline, worry) in your life
Reach your root to the stream once today
Say: 'I don't fear the heat; my root is by the water'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to be your stream in this season's heat
Thank Him for leaves that stay green anyway

verse.text: They drank from the spiritual rock that accompanied them, and that rock was Christ.

blocks.text: In the wilderness, Israel drank from water out of a rock — and Paul quietly reveals who the rock was. The water that followed them through the desert was Christ. Your stream was there in your wildernesses before you even knew to look. The Rock has been accompanying you the whole time, ready to give water.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Look back: when did God provide 'water' you didn't expect?
See the Rock who has accompanied you
Drink — receive from Him today

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Christ, the Rock who has walked with you
Ask to know His water in your current wilderness

verse.text: For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light.

blocks.text: Rivers have sources, and the source of every good river is one fountain. 'With you is the fountain of life' — the spring deep behind your season. And look at the line's end: 'in your light we see light.' Everything bright you've ever enjoyed is reflected brightness. Your life's water all traces back to one living fountain.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Trace one good thing in your life back to its source
Worship at the fountain, not the stream
Say: 'with You is the fountain of life'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God that He is the source behind all sources
Ask to keep drinking where life actually comes from

verse.text: The righteous will flourish like a palm tree, they will grow like a cedar of Lebanon; planted in the house of the Lord, they will flourish in the courts of our God.

blocks.text: Quiz day — and this verse shows where the best trees are planted: in the courtyard of God's house, right where the water and the care gather. The righteous don't just survive; they flourish. Check what you remember about life by the water.

blocks.question: Where do the righteous flourish, according to Psalm 92:13?
options: In the deep woods far from anyone
In the house of the Lord, in the courts of God
On the dry hillside where they look dramatic
In the richest soil they can buy
blocks.explain: Psalm 92:13: 'planted in the house of the Lord, they will flourish in the courts of our God.' The best planting spot is near God's presence and God's people.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to flourish where God plants you
Thank Him for a house with roots-room in it

verse.text: The Lord will guide you always; he will satisfy your needs in a sun-scorched land and will strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden.

blocks.text: Rest day for the water tree. 'Well-watered' is your identity. Even in sun-scorched land, God satisfies needs and strengthens frames — the water is not a hope, it's a promise. Today, don't work for the garden; be the garden. Let the water arrive.

blocks.prompt: When have you felt most 'well-watered'? What does your soul look like when it's satisfied instead of scorched?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Be the well-watered garden, not the worried gardener
Thank God for satisfaction in a scorched land

verse.text: There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God, the holy place where the Most High dwells.

blocks.text: Three weeks left — and we end the water week inside the city. The river's streams 'make glad' — not just supply, but gladden. The water tree is not sustained and miserable; it's sustained and glad. Let week 11 end with rivers making your heart glad. That's what all this deep-rooted living is for.

blocks.prompt: Where has joy come from being planted by streams? What has this season's 'water' made glad in you?
blocks.placeholder: The water has made me glad because...

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Let the river's streams make you glad
Thank the Most High for dwelling in such a city

intro.text: A tree's story is written in its rings — wide years and narrow years, good rain and drought. This week we learn to read seasons: the time for everything, and the patience to trust God with the calendar.

verse.text: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens.

blocks.text: The most freeing calendar is God's calendar: a time for everything. A time to grow and a time to rest. A time to speak and a time to be quiet. The reason life feels out of rhythm is usually that we're trying to do one season in another — blooming in winter, sleeping in spring. Ask what time it actually is for you.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name your current 'season' — growing, waiting, pruning, resting?
Stop fighting the season you're in
Do what today's season calls for, not last month's

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to show you what time it is
Thank Him for a season for everything

verse.text: He has made everything beautiful in its time.

blocks.text: The same verse right after 'a time for everything' holds the comfort: everything beautiful in its time. Not beautiful on your schedule. The ring you can't see the beauty of yet is the one being drawn slowly in the dark. God sees the whole tree at every age; He declares each season beautiful at its proper time.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Find one 'ugly now' part of your year and ask God to show its purpose
Trust that beauty is scheduled, not missing
Say: 'He has made everything beautiful in its time'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Tell God the season you can't see beauty in yet
Thank Him for a beauty that waits for its time

verse.text: Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom.

blocks.text: Every tree knows its days are numbered; that's why it makes rings instead of putting everything into one afternoon. 'Teach us to number our days' is not morbid — it's how you get wisdom. When you know the season has a number and a limit, you spend it on things that matter. Each day is a ring you're adding.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Look at a tree ring or a calendar — count ahead
Ask: am I using what's numbered like it's numbered?
Give this day a purpose worth a ring

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for the wisdom of numbered days
Thank God for the days He's given you to count

verse.text: He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rains that water the earth.

blocks.text: Hard seasons end — that's the quiet promise in this verse. The Lord comes to us 'like the spring rains that water the earth.' Spring always returns to the garden. If your rings have been drought-thin for a while, there is still rain on the calendar. God's arrival refreshes; He doesn't just command the ground to try harder.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Wait like a farmer for God's timing, not yours
Don't panic at the drought; watch for the rain
Say: 'He comes to me like spring rains'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask for spring rain where you've been dry
Thank God that He comes as rain, not just requirement

verse.text: See how the farmer waits for the land to yield its valuable crop, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains.

blocks.text: Quiz day on patience. The farmer is the Bible's favorite picture of wise waiting — he doesn't check on every seed every hour, and he doesn't dig the whole field looking for progress. He waits for both rains and trusts the land. Here's today's check: how do you read your own rings?

blocks.question: In James 5:7, the farmer waits for the crop patiently. He waits for what two things?
options: Autumn and spring rains
Warmer days and longer nights
New tools and hired workers
Morning and evening watering
blocks.explain: 'He waits for the land to yield its valuable crop, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains.' The farmer trusts a rhythm he can depend on — and so can you.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask to wait like the farmer, not like a panicked manager
Thank God for the autumn and spring of your seasons

verse.text: He made the moon to mark the seasons, and the sun knows when to go down.

blocks.text: Rest day — and the excuse is cosmic: God timed the moon and the sun, making the whole sky a calendar of rest and rhythm. Night comes so rest can come. The moon marks the seasons so you can trust the turn. Rest beneath the order God built instead of fighting it.

blocks.prompt: What season marker have you noticed lately — the day shortening, the sky, a birthday? What is it saying about where you are?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Rest under God's ordered sky
Thank Him for moons and seasons that mark your life

verse.text: Your beginnings will seem humble, so prosperous will your future be.

blocks.text: Most great trees had laughable first rings. Job's friend Bildad — who got a lot wrong — got this line exactly right: humble beginnings, prosperous future. Your first ring doesn't dictate your last one. Sown in a small beginning, overtaking with growth — that's how God writes a season. End week 12 with hope about the rings still coming.

blocks.prompt: What is one humble beginning God might be growing now toward something thriving? What's your best guess at the 'ring' you're in?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for your humble beginnings
Ask Him for the prosperous rings He has planned

intro.text: One tree is an achievement; a grove is a community. We finish the season by standing beside each other — roots that grow toward each other, shade that shelters someone else, and a whole forest that sings.

verse.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

blocks.text: The grove's first law is Jesus' own summary of His whole giving life: the giver is the blessed one. A grove doesn't hoard its fruit or its shade; trees give away their leaves every autumn and call it a good year. As you end this season, ask what you've become — a taker in the grove, or a giver?

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give something today that costs you a little
Notice whose joy becomes yours
Say: 'I am built to give, like my Lord'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank Jesus for the giver-hearted life
Ask to be more blessed by giving than keeping

verse.text: Yet when planted, it grows up and becomes the largest of all garden plants, with such big branches that the birds can perch in its shade.

blocks.text: The tiniest seed of the season grows into a tree big enough for birds to perch in its shade. Notice the tree's reward — birds. Not applause, not prizes, birds. The purpose of bigness is shelter. The larger your root system grew this season, the more people should be able to rest under your life.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Name one 'bird' — someone who needs shade
Let your maturity cast a shadow that helps them
Remember: shelter, not show, is what bigness is for

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make you big enough to shelter
Thank Him for the birds He will send to your shade

verse.text: Therefore encourage one another and build each other up.

blocks.text: Trees in a grove interlock roots; people in God's family encourage each other. 'Encourage' literally means to put courage in. A grove that doesn't speak to its trees grows a forest of loners. Your words are root connections. Say one honest, specific, building thing to someone today — it travels to their root.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Give one specific, sincere encouragement (not flattery)
Say it to a fellow 'tree' in your family or church
Do it again tomorrow — groves do this weekly

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to make your words root-connections
Thank Him for the people who build you up

verse.text: You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.

blocks.text: We end close to where we began — only now the picture is bigger. One tree becomes a garden; one well becomes a spring. The whole season's growth was never about you becoming a perfect single tree. It was about you joining a grove, a garden, a spring that waters everything around it. You are part of something with more fruit than one branch can carry.

blocks.title: Try it today
items: Look at your season as a whole — count how much grew
See yourself as part of the garden, not the whole orchard
Say: 'I am a spring whose waters never fail'

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the garden you're planted in
Ask to be a spring that feeds the whole grove

verse.text: Therefore, as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people, especially to those who belong to the family of believers.

blocks.text: Final quiz of the season, and here's the question behind it: thirteen weeks of roots, and where does it all go? The answer is out, toward all people — with a special priority to God's family. A grove doesn't keep good for its own roots. Check what you remember, then let the season spill out.

blocks.question: After a whole season of growing roots, where does God's goodness travel?
options: Backward, into saving yourself
Upward, into feeling holy
Outward, doing good to all people
Sideways, only among close friends
blocks.explain: Galatians 6:10: 'as we have opportunity, let us do good to all people.' Deep roots did their work over thirteen weeks — now the fruit moves outward, toward everyone.

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Ask God to direct the season's growth outward
Thank Him for the whole family of believers to love

verse.text: Let the fields be jubilant, and everything in them; let all the trees of the forest sing for joy.

blocks.text: The last rest day of the season — and the forest itself sings. You don't need to do anything today. The grove is already celebrating. When your season ends well, the trees around you catch it. Sit with the people you belong to and let the whole forest make music.

blocks.prompt: If the trees of the forest sang for joy today, which 'tree' in your life would provide the best harmony? What song is your season singing?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Join the forest in singing
Thank God for a grove worth rejoicing in

verse.text: ...down the middle of the great street of the city. On each side of the river stood the tree of life, bearing twelve crops of fruit, yielding its fruit every month.

blocks.text: The last verse of the season points to the last tree of the story: the tree of life in the city, bearing fruit every month, its leaves for the healing of the nations. Everything you grew this spring — every root, every ring, every fruit — is training for that tree. The end of the season is the beginning of the eternal grove. Finish well.

blocks.prompt: Thirteen weeks done. What did God grow in you this season? What do you want to keep doing daily, even after the guide ends?

blocks.title: Pray it today
items: Thank God for the whole season of root-growing
Ask to keep bearing fruit, month after month
